description: Three platforms use different project instruction files. Investigate: Can one file serve all? Can they reference a common source? How to maintain parity with minimal duplication.
notes:
COMPLETED. Findings:

PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS:
- CONFIRMED: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md at project root. Auto-loaded. Markdown format.
- CONFIRMED: OpenCode reads opencode.md referenced in opencode.json instructions array. Also supports file://rules/*.md glob patterns.

A) Three separate files maintained in parallel -- high duplication, drift risk.
B) One canonical file (e.g., PROJECT.md) that each platform file includes/references.

The project-level instruction files (CLAUDE.md, opencode.md, AGENTS.md) differ mainly in platform-specific references (hooks, tools, agent invocation). Keep a shared core + thin platform wrappers.

ACTUALLY BETTER: Since the content is mostly identical, maintain a single PROJECT.md (or just CLAUDE.md as canonical since tackline started there) and symlink/copy to the other two names. Platform-specific content goes in a 'Platform Notes' section at the end.
